latest_apis.rationale: The app is on the newest stable release of both the framework and its adapter, and every API it touches (params, request/response, set:html, is:inline, script/component conventions) is the current generation — nothing legacy-era in the codebase. The only current framework primitive not used is Astro 7's route caching, which is a reasonable omission since the spec requires live data and the app needs shared data caching, not response caching.

app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:307-342 — table sorting with aria-sort, dataset, tBodies, native buttons/selects

platform.rationale: Reaches for the platform first everywhere — native form controls, DOMParser, URLSearchParams, CSS custom properties, no polyfills or libraries — which is the ideal fit for Astro's zero-JS model. Docked one point because the server fetches have no AbortSignal/timeout (pokeapi.js:35) and stale client requests are guarded with a sequence counter instead of AbortController, plus a full location.reload() on popstate (index.astro:190).

dependencies.rationale: Minimal and modern: only the framework and its adapter, both current, with no client framework, utility library, CSS framework or state library despite a rich spec that would have tempted one.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokeapi.js:1-139 — all API access, caching, and card assembly behind one well-defined module; no page touches fetch directly
app/astro.config.mjs:1-6 — six-line config, one place for all framework configuration, no experimental flags or internals

app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:35-42,228 — evolution chain built as hand-escaped HTML strings injected with set:html instead of a recursive Astro component: an escapeHtml surface that would churn with the framework's own escaping
app/src/pages/abilities/[name].astro:31-52 — card assembly duplicated from cardsFromPokemonRefs (pokeapi.js:118-139) rather than parameterized, so a card-shape change touches two sites
app/src/lib/pokeapi.js — untyped .js despite Astro's native TypeScript support, so upstream API shape changes surface as runtime errors, not type errors
churn_resistance.rationale: A framework or adapter upgrade would touch almost nothing, and data access is centralized to a degree that makes the API itself replaceable. The deductions are localized future-churn risks: the hand-built HTML string renderer, one duplicated card-assembly path, and an untyped boundary against a large external API.

findings.issue: Evolution chain is rendered by building HTML strings with a hand-rolled escapeHtml and injecting via set:html (:228), instead of using Astro's templating, which escapes automatically
findings.suggestion: Write a small recursive .astro component (or a <ul> mapped in markup) for chain nodes so escaping is handled by the framework and the escapeHtml helper can be deleted

findings.issue: Server-side fetch has no timeout or abort, so a hung upstream request hangs the page render indefinitely, and the in-flight promise is cached
findings.suggestion: Pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)` to fetch() and clear the cached promise on abort (the existing catch-based eviction already covers it)

findings.issue: Pokémon-card assembly (species filter, dedupe by species, sprite/name extraction) is a near-copy of cardsFromPokemonRefs in app/src/lib/pokeapi.js:118-139
findings.suggestion: Extend cardsFromPokemonRefs with an optional per-entry transform so the hidden-ability flag flows through the shared helper

findings.issue: The entire data layer is plain JavaScript with no types at the API boundary, despite Astro supporting TypeScript natively
findings.suggestion: Rename to pokeapi.ts and type the PokeAPI record shapes actually consumed (names, genera, varieties, version_group_details), so upstream API changes fail at compile time

findings.issue: Stale responses are guarded by a sequence counter instead of aborting the superseded request, and popstate triggers a full location.reload() (:190)
findings.suggestion: Keep one AbortController per request and abort the previous one on new input; on popstate, reuse the same refresh() path with a replaceState instead of reloading

findings.issue: Astro 7's stabilized route caching (memoryCache() provider, routeRules, Astro.cache — added in astro@7.0.0) is not configured; caching is entirely hand-rolled
findings.suggestion: Not required by the spec's live-data constraint, but adding `cache: { provider: memoryCache() }` plus short routeRules maxAge for the heavy list pages would cut re-render cost on repeat visits

summary: This app ages well: it sits on the newest stable Astro (7.4.4, the current release) with only two first-party dependencies, uses only current-generation framework APIs, and pushes interactivity onto the platform (fetch/DOMParser/URLSearchParams/native controls) rather than adding a client framework. All data access is centralized in one module with a thoughtful runtime cache, so API or framework changes would touch few files. The main future-churn risks are a hand-escaped HTML-string renderer for the evolution tree, an untyped data layer, and one duplicated card-assembly path — all small, localized fixes.
